text: The override re-places one instruction: the current partner_instruction of the case ends at RECALLED and a new partner_instruction is created at SENT with the chosen partner, the same instruction type and the due date. The two status names are values of LOV-INSTR-STATUS, and no transition table of that list, no second table and no status value outside the list is declared.
why: TSD S9 T3.2 publishes LOV-INSTR-STATUS with SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and RECALLED and no source publishes the transitions between them; the legacy feature asks only that work be placed differently, so ending the old placement and creating the new one uses published values and adds no record type. Inventing a status or a table would add a business value and a migration no document owns.
read: TSD S9 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S9 A2.4.2; legacy RWB-E6-032 Story, Acceptance criteria and Data; context pack ownership rows (table partner_instruction); Template and Rules v1 R9
applied_in: RWB-S9-E6032-APP sections 1, 2, 4, 8 BR1, 9 and 11; RWB-S9-E6032-CON sections 2, 7 AC2 and AC5, 8 BR7, 9 and 11
confirm: Business lead and the solution architect, before wave 4 starts
impact: The override runs on the existing one-table model with two status moves and no migration, and a build that adds a status or a placement table fails the contract review

text: The override is served by the published POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions (API-S9-002) with partner-portal right C and the Idempotency-Key header, and its reason is one additive optional property of InstructionRequest named overrideReason, with the 1000-character limit of the published DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason. No override path, override element or override flag is declared, and the request's own required flags are not published, so the override branch requires partnerId, instructionType and overrideReason itself.
why: The six published operations of the service place work through API-S9-002 only and none is an override; the legacy endpoints the story lists place no work at all. The reason has a published home on the decision-log element and no published home on the instruction request, so an additive optional property is the smallest change that keeps major version 1 and invents no business value.
read: TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; API Specification v4 InstructionRequest, PartnerInstruction and DecisionLogEntry; context pack ownership rows (6 REST operations); legacy RWB-E6-032 Endpoints; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and ADR-020
applied_in: RWB-S9-E6032-APP sections 2, 4, 8 BR3 and BR10, 12.1, 12.3 and 13; RWB-S9-E6032-CON sections 2, 7 AC1 and AC2, 8 BR3 and BR5, 11 and 12.1
confirm: Solution architect, the business lead and the rwb-partner tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: One branch and one additive property on the published operation, no new path, and the addition stays inside major version 1

text: The reason is written to the local decision record as overrideReason and to the decision_log_entry element of rwb-decision; partner_instruction has no reason column and this story adds none, so the reason's field ID, list and value format carry the placeholder and the reason is free text of up to 1000 characters.
why: TSD S9 T3.1 gives partner_instruction the nine columns DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 with no reason, FSD S9 A2.4.3.2 lists the partner fields and the two instruction keys only, and the API Specification v4 publishes DecisionLogEntry.overrideReason as the reason taken when a person does not follow a recommendation. Adding a column or an enumeration would invent a business value, and dropping the reason would lose the legacy requirement.

text: The override publishes and consumes no event: EV-20 InstructionIssued belongs to the step that first issues an instruction, EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted is the result step's trigger and, per the Event and Messaging Design v4, is consumed from the partner portal. The outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as a missing H row, and the disagreement between TSD S9 T5.3 (both events Published) and the event catalogue (EV-21 Consumed) is recorded rather than resolved by a declaration.
why: The ownership rows give the service two events that carry an issue and a portal result, the pattern set carries no DP-09, and the two source documents disagree on EV-21's direction. A step that re-places an instruction can announce nothing without the outbox row this plan does not hold, and picking one direction would silently drop the other source.
read: Context pack ownership rows (events EV-20 and EV-21) and service row (topic rwb.partner.events.v1); Event and Messaging Design v4 rows EV-20 and EV-21; TSD S9 T5.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14, R3 source precedence

text: The override is authorised on the partner-portal right C that TSD S9 T-A.1 declares: T6.1 gives C to seven identities, RW-AGENCYMG (CRUDA), RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE and RW-GUARANT (CRU), while RW-CASEOWN and the other bank roles hold R and the six PT-* portal identities hold RU. The legacy permission table's right U, its 21 further holders of R and its 5 further holders of U are recorded as the narrower legacy reading and are not enumerated as new rights.

Taking the matrix alone refuses the portal identities, and granting a new right or listing unnamed holders would invent access rows.
